paragraphs: Every London borough runs its own fostering service, and more and more of them recruit together. In May 2024 fourteen boroughs combined their recruitment: Waltham Forest, Barking and Dagenham, Havering, Newham, Redbridge and Tower Hamlets as Local Community Fostering in the north-east, and Brent, Ealing, Hammersmith and Fulham, Harrow, Hillingdon, Hounslow, Kensington and Chelsea and Westminster as Foster with West London. In the north, Barnet, Camden, Enfield, Hackney, Haringey and Islington have worked together since 2012 and now share the North London Fostering Hub, led by Camden. Alongside the councils, the independent agencies shown above approve and support carers across the capital.

The two routes work differently. A borough approves you itself and places its own children with you. An independent agency assesses, trains and supervises you, and councils ask it to find homes for the children they look after. Compare the training and support each offers as well as the pay.

The shortage is plain in the official figures. When the fourteen boroughs launched, Tower Hamlets said there were four children in the capital needing a foster place for every approved carer, and that approved fostering households had fallen from 3,685 in 2014 to 2,560 at the end of March 2023. Ofsted's figures for the year to March 2025, as reported by the Barnet Post, showed 2,425 council fostering households in London, down from 3,365 in 2020-21. London councils approved about 240 new households that year, up from 190, while about 270 stopped fostering.

Space is often the hurdle. Children aged two and over need a bedroom of their own, and one in three people asked in a 2024 Foster Care Fortnight survey said they did not have the room. The North London hub expects the government's Room Makers scheme, which funds changes to a home that create extra space, to be extended to every fostering hub. Some boroughs add their own help: from 2026-27 Tower Hamlets is refunding Council Tax in full to newly approved carers at the end of their first year.

If you have a spare room, talk to your own borough and to two or three of the agencies above before you choose. The pages for Croydon, Barnet, Newham and Tower Hamlets, among other boroughs, list the services covering each part of London.
